nodes.description: Standard first-line combination antituberculous therapy. A Hong Kong trial in 240 men with silicotuberculosis found more relapses with 6 months than 8 months of thrice-weekly streptomycin, isoniazid, rifampicin and pyrazinamide, so at least 8 months is advised; a South African trial of short-course therapy found it adequate, so the need for a longer regimen is not settled. The treatment trials used older regimens.

nodes.description: Treatment of latent tuberculosis infection in people with silicosis. Isoniazid, or isoniazid plus rifampicin, roughly halved the proportion developing tuberculosis in a Hong Kong placebo-controlled trial, though substantial residual risk remained; WHO strongly recommends systematic testing and treatment of latent infection in people with silicosis. Rifampicin plus pyrazinamide carried more hepatotoxicity than isoniazid. Mass community preventive therapy in gold miners did not reduce tuberculosis at the population level once treatment ended.
nodes.id: Tuberculosis preventive therapy for latent infection

evidence.reference_title: Management of latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection: WHO guidelines for low tuberculosis burden countries.
